beliefs.practice: Use a single shared MongoClient instance (a singleton) created at app startup and reused across modules; do not open a new client per request. Close the client gracefully on shutdown.

Read the cluster connection string and all credentials from environment variables (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a config secret store; never commit credentials into source, logs, or seed files. Provide a .env.example with placeholders only.
Enforce TLS/SSL for connections and validate server certificates (enable TLS/ssl options in the driver and supply CA or system trust); do not disable certificate validation to avoid MITM risk.

Tune the MongoDB driver pool and timeouts for the managed cluster: set an appropriate maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS and heartbeatFrequencyMS to match the cluster size and client concurrency; document chosen values and rationale.
Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and retryable server responses; limit retry count and classify errors so non-idempotent operations are not retried blindly.
Make logging of outcomes idempotent (use upsert or a unique outcome key) so retries or duplicate orchestrator runs do not create duplicate records.

Create an index on the cart abandonment timestamp field (e.g., abandonedAt or lastUpdated) and include any filter fields (status, channelPreference) as a compound index so the query 'abandoned > 2 hours AND status = X' is index-supported.
Use projections to return only the fields needed for orchestration (customer id, contact, preference, cart items, embedding) to reduce network usage and memory pressure.
Batch or bulk-write logs and status updates (use bulkWrite with ordered:false) instead of many single writes to reduce latency and RU/IOPS consumption.

For vector similarity, store embeddings as a fixed-dimension numeric array and create the appropriate vector index (DiskANN / HNSW / IVF) on the embedding field with tuned index params (e.g., M, efConstruction) appropriate for the data volume and latency targets.
Normalize and persist the embedding dimensionality and datatype (e.g., float32, fixed length) and validate at write-time so vector index queries always receive consistent vectors.
When calling LLM or external channels, keep secrets (OPENAI_API_KEY etc.) out of the database; read them from environment or secret store and implement key rotation and limited scope credentials.
Seed scripts must be idempotent: use upserts or check-for-existence rather than dropping collections so the script is safe to run against the sample database repeatedly.

Use the provider’s explain/monitoring tools (documentdb MCP server or explain() plans) to verify that the critical queries (abandoned cart search) use indexes and do not trigger full collection scans.
Provision adequate throughput for queries and bulk writes (use autoscale where available) and monitor RU/s (or equivalent) consumption; tune indices and batching to control cost.
Design the orchestrator as idempotent and resilient to duplicates: mark carts as 'processing' with a timestamp and a worker id, use lease timeouts, and safely recover or requeue abandoned leases.
When multiple writes must be atomic across docs/collections, use multi-document transactions if supported by the cluster/version; otherwise use compensating operations or idempotent updates.

Use least-privilege database users/roles for application access (create a user limited to the sample_retail_12 DB and to required operations) rather than a cluster admin connection string embedded in the app.
Avoid fetching large cart item arrays if not needed for copy generation; instead fetch a summarized view or top N items to keep LLM prompts small and reduce document transfer size.
Index and normalize the customer channel preference field and contact details so routing logic (email vs SMS) is a cheap indexed filter rather than a full-document scan.
Validate and enforce a schema (MongoDB collection validator) for carts and outcome logs to prevent malformed documents and make queries predictable.
Use correlation IDs in logs and database records to trace a cart through copy-generation, channel sending, and DB logging for observability and debugging across distributed calls.
When performing similarity queries, limit the search to a reasonable topK and use approximate search parameters (efSearch/ef) to control latency and RU consumption; evaluate recall vs cost.
Monitor index cardinality and avoid indexing high-cardinality free-text fields without need; prefer specialized text index or external search for heavy full‑text needs.
Implement graceful shutdown and signal handling in the Node.js CLI (SIGINT/SIGTERM): stop polling, wait for in-flight LLM or channel calls, flush pending DB writes, and close the MongoClient.
